topic: The Fish That Fuses With Its Mate
centralQuestion: How can a male triplewart seadevil permanently fuse with a female while remaining reproductively functional?
thesis: In the triplewart seadevil, a male can permanently join a female through fused tissue and vascular connections, gaining nutrition while retaining his reproductive role; reproductive assurance is an evolutionary explanation.
viewerPayoff: In the triplewart seadevil, a male can permanently join a female through fused tissue and vascular connections, gaining nutrition while retaining his reproductive role; reproductive assurance is an evolutionary explanation.

visualOpportunities.title: Skin contact to vascular connection
visualOpportunities.description: Large female occupies frame with tiny male beside her ventral flank; short lure,3 dorsal caruncles and jaw establish species. Camera closes immediately; no empty water opening. Track a large-eyed, lureless male swimming through black water; restrained distant point of female light and huge female silhouette emerge. Search direction is illustrative, not a proven tracking path. Reveal entire same female at near-profile angle; three dorsal caruncles, tiny female eye, small pectoral and short esca remain visible. Scientific species label. Continuous close-in approach ending with both jaw tips physically against female ventral skin; tiny hooked denticles visible only in macro. Hold the grip, no immediate vascular join. Camera enters the contact seam. Two adjoining tissue surfaces become continuous across a narrow junction; vascular lumen connection develops only later. Organic connected tissue, not floating cell grid. Follow illustrative paired vessel paths across the same narrow seam and into the recognizable male. Warm flow motion means nutrient transport only. Male remains whole; no detailed internal organ map or sperm-in-blood imagery. Pull out from seam to show male retained externally, with body and fin movement; no shrinking into organ or disappearance. Macro seam remains anatomically joined; secondary restrained visual distinction between intact tissue and absent rejection attack, no literal immune cells being switched off. Large adaptive-immunity label plus evolved-gene-loss qualification. Camera orbits joined tissue toward exterior. Both fish remain distinct. Research qualification legible; no pathogens, shields or speculative defense pathways. Return to matched opening view of attached pair in huge dark water column; camera widens while pair stays physically connected. No egg or sperm release not directly verified for species. Final gentle orbit of joined pair, female moves and male follows at exact attachment point; resolve first image with lasting physical association, no single-individual or love metaphor.
